turns.content: Five families splitting a 2500 cabin evenly. That means each owes 500 flat, right

**Yes.** 2500 ÷ 5 = 500, so each family owes 500 if the total is exactly 2500 and the split is equal with no extras.

That holds only for a flat total of 2500 with no taxes, fees, deposits, or uneven usage. If any of those apply, the per-family amount changes.
Right. Lodge just sent a binding addendum. One room flooded, repriced to 100. They re-invoiced the other four rooms at 600 each. So total is still 2500.

The lodge total is still 2500 (100 + 4 × 600), so an even five-way split of that total is still 500 per family.

That 500 is only the group-equalization number. It is not the lodge invoice: one room is billed 100, four rooms 600 each.

If the families still settle the cabin evenly, each nets 500: the flooded-room party paid 100 and would transfer 400 to the others; each of the other four paid 600 and would get 100 back. If each pays only its lodge invoice, the shares are 100 and 600, not 500.

Which of those applies depends on whether the original even-split agreement still governs after the addendum, not on the total remaining 2500.

The lodge did not bill five families 500. It billed one room 100 and four rooms 600. An even split of the 2500 **total** is still 500 per family only as an internal settlement, and only if that agreement still stands. A group message that just bills everyone 500, without those invoice amounts, would be false.

Lodge addendum: one room flooded and is now 100; the other four rooms are 600 each. Total is still 2500.

If we keep an even five-way split of that total, each family’s share is 500. That is not the lodge invoice.

To land at 500 each: the family on the 100 invoice pays the lodge 100 and transfers 400 into the group; each family on a 600 invoice pays the lodge 600 and is owed 100 back. Confirm who is on which invoice and who has already paid the lodge before anyone transfers.
